docs.title: Security model at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph people [" "]
        A["Admin / Developer / Approver"]
    end
    A -->|"session auth (HTTPS)"| CP["Secrets Bridge Control Plane<br/>(metadata • workflow • audit • RBAC)"]
    CP -->|"outbound jobs only"| AG["Secrets Bridge Agent<br/>(inside your boundary)"]
    AG -->|"read / write values"| P["External Provider<br/>AWS SM · Vault · Azure KV · GCP SM · Kubernetes"]
  • The agent is outbound-only: it opens connections to the control plane and to its local provider; it never accepts inbound connections.
  • The agent accepts no inbound connections for control-plane or user traffic. Its only listener serves health probes and metrics; the Helm chart binds it on the pod IP for kubelet and its NetworkPolicy denies all ingress.
  • The agent has no Postgres and no Redis dependency, and no Kubernetes API access to read or write Secrets.
  • The control plane stores metadata only, never plaintext values.
  • Secrets remain in the provider. Secrets Bridge governs access around them.
  • Values move only through controlled, wrapped, single-shot flows (KMS-wrapped envelopes, consumed exactly once, short TTL).
  • Audit is metadata-only: actions, IDs, statuses, reasons, timestamps; no values, tokens, or wrap bodies.

See the full architecture and the threat model for how each boundary is enforced.

docs.title: The guarantees we hold
docs.text:
• Outbound-only agent: no inbound listener apart from the probe and metrics port, no cluster-API dependency.
  • Metadata-only audit: append-only at the schema layer (Postgres triggers).
  • No plaintext persistence: not in Postgres, Redis, logs, or the browser.
  • MFA-gated reveal: non-prod reveals require an MFA step-up.
  • Prod reveal hard-block: refused and audited, not merely discouraged.
  • One-time enrollment tokens: hash-only, short-TTL, returned once, spent once.
  • Provider-bound agents: an enrolled agent is bound to a single provider connection.
  • Revocation: an agent can be revoked; its heartbeats and job polling stop being accepted immediately.

docs.title: Teams and section heads
docs.text: Most organisations don't fit cleanly into a flat list of projects. A real engineering org has sections, sub-teams, leads, and members, and the people at each level need access to their part of the world, no more and no less. The platform models this with a first-class team tree: an N-level hierarchy where role grants scoped to a team automatically fan out through that team's entire subtree.

docs.title: The model
docs.text: Three entities, one rule.

docs.title: teams: the tree
docs.text:
Each team carries a name, optional description, status (active / archived), and a nullable parent_team_id. Root teams have no parent; everything else is a descendant. The depth is N. The schema doesn't impose a limit.

acme
├── platform
│   ├── platform-east
│   └── platform-west
└── security
    └── security-compliance

Sibling names must be unique under the same parent. acme/platform/ops and acme/security/ops are both fine; two ops under acme/platform are not. The constraint is per-parent, so renaming or re-parenting never breaks cousins.

A team cannot be deleted while it has children; unparent or delete those first. team_members rows cascade-delete with the team they belong to (the user account stays; only the membership row goes).

docs.title: team_members: who belongs
docs.text: A simple (team_id, user_id) join. Structural only: membership does NOT grant any permission on its own. The platform deliberately keeps "who you are" and "what you can do" in two tables so you can reorganise teams without rewriting RBAC.

docs.title: Role grants scoped to a team
docs.text:
The connecting tissue. A row in user_roles carries a scope JSON object; setting scope.team_id = <team> tells the access resolver "this grant applies to that team's entire subtree".

{
  "user_id": "alice",
  "role_id": "<approver-role>",
  "scope": { "team_id": "acme/platform" }
}

Alice is now an approver for everything inside platform and every descendant team. She can approve platform-east and platform-west requests, and requests for a new sub-team created under platform tomorrow, with no follow-up grant needed.

docs.title: The "section head" pattern
docs.text:
A common shape this model unlocks:

  1. Build the tree under /admin/teams. Reflect your org chart: a top-level team per section, child teams per squad, grandchild teams if you have feature pods.
  2. Assign projects to teams by setting project.team_id on create (or via PUT /projects/:id/team after). This is the wiring that lets the access resolver expand a team-scoped grant into a set of accessible projects.
  3. Grant the section head on /admin/assignments: pick the user, pick the role (secret.approve for an approver, secret.list + secret.request for a developer-style lead), and pick the section team in the Team dropdown. Leave Project unset; the team scope makes it implicit.

That single grant produces this behaviour:

The section head's view How it works /secrets shows every secret bound to every project under their section EffectiveProjectAccess expands team_id → descendant teams (recursive CTE) → projects with team_id in that set /requests lists requests from any project under their section Same expansion, filtered server-side Approve / Reject works for any of those requests The approve gate runs checkApproverScope with the same resolver Approve / Reject refuses on any request OUTSIDE their subtree Returns 403 with the stable string out_of_scope_project New sub-team added later under their section Auto-covered, no follow-up grant Project re-assigned to a different team Auto-shifts in/out of scope, no manual cleanup

docs.title: How requests respect the scope
docs.text:
The check fires at submit time AND at approve time, on top of the normal secret.list / secret.request / secret.approve permission check:

  • Submit gate: Requests.WithTenancyGate validates the caller's secret.request grants cover the request's project_id, op is in the binding's allowed_ops, and every requested key is in allowed_keys (when non-null). Stable errors: out_of_scope_project, out_of_scope_op, out_of_scope_key.
  • Approve gate: checkApproverScope validates the voter's secret.approve grants cover the request's project_id. Same team-subtree expansion as the submit gate.

Both gates have the same back-compat behaviour: legacy requests whose TargetScope["project_id"] isn't a UUID bypass the team check (so installs without scoped projects keep working byte-for-byte).

docs.title: How the UI uses this
docs.text:
The SPA hydrates a single /users/me call after login:

{
  "id":           "<uuid>",
  "email":        "alice@example.com",
  "display_name": "Alice",
  "permissions":  ["secret.list", "secret.request", "secret.approve", "..."],
  "teams":        [{"id":"...","name":"platform","parent_team_id":null,"status":"active"}],
  "projects":     [{"id":"...","name":"Billing","status":"active"}]
}
  • Sidebar items gate on the permissions array. The admin section hides entirely if no admin permission is held; individual nav items hide if their gating permission is missing.
  • /secrets is filtered server-side to only the projects in projects (or every project if the caller holds a global grant).
  • Submit drawer defaults to "From my bindings" mode for scoped users: pick a project from projects, pick one of its bound secrets, the form auto-fills provider type + ref + the allowed-ops / allowed-keys constraints. Admins (holders of team.edit) start on the free-form mode for onboarding new bindings.
  • /me profile page renders the full payload: identity, the permission set, direct team memberships, and the accessible projects, all read from the same AuthContext.

Permission gating is strictly fail-closed: until /users/me returns, hasPermission(...) is false for every key. A session restored from sessionStorage shows the Dashboard + a "Loading permissions…" line while the request is in flight; there is no flash of admin nav for non-admins on rehydration.

docs.title: Practical advice
docs.text:
• Keep teams shallow when you can. Two or three levels covers most orgs. The recursive CTE handles depth N just fine, but a flatter tree is easier for admins to reason about.
  • Don't reuse team_members as a permission system. Membership is structural metadata. Always grant capabilities via a role + scope.
  • Archive instead of delete when a team is being wound down. The status flag preserves audit trails: requests filed against projects in an archived team subtree still resolve. Delete only when the team is truly empty and the historical references are no longer interesting.
  • A grant can target both project_id and team_id in the same scope object. The resolver computes the union, so a user can be "the section head over platform" PLUS "co-owner of one specific project in security" via two separate grant rows or one combined scope.
  • Free-form mode in the submit drawer still works. It's the default for admins, who are usually the ones submitting the first request against a brand-new binding. The api-side gate is the same in both modes; bound mode is a UX overlay that keeps scoped users from constructing requests that would 403.

docs.title: Threat model & hard rules
docs.text: These are the rules the project never breaks. They're enforced where possible by tests, schema constraints, and CI greps; where that isn't possible, code review is the gate.

docs.title: Value-bearing data
docs.text: Rule How it's enforced Secret values never appear in Postgres outside the KMS envelope TestWrap_PlaintextNotInDB scans encrypted_value for the plaintext canary Secret values never appear in Redis The pkg/runtime package doesn't expose a generic Set(key, value): only idempotency tokens, locks, rate-limit windows, pub/sub messages Secret values never appear in audit metadata Service layer audits byte_length + SHA-256 content_hash only; TestWrap_AuditTrailHashesContentNotValue scans the audit metadata column for the canary Secret values never appear in API responses Wire shapes in internal/handlers/* deliberately omit value fields; the request response carries target_keys (names) only Secret values never persisted in the browser The SPA writes nothing to localStorage / sessionStorage / IndexedDB. The only cookie is the HttpOnly sb_session cookie the api sets, which page scripts can't read

docs.title: Provider credentials
docs.text: Rule How it's enforced Provider credentials never leave the agent's network boundary The CP doesn't have any column or field that could hold one; the agent's resolvers refuse credential-shaped keys in the payload (e.g. seven banned aws*Key* names) Provider credentials never in frontend code The UI talks only to the Control Plane API; there's no provider SDK in the SPA's dependency tree ArgoCD tokens (for §26 observation) are KMS-wrapped at rest Stored in argocd_endpoints.token_ciphertext (BYTEA) via the same KeyManager used for secret_wraps; canary scan returns zero hits

docs.title: Append-only audit
docs.text: Rule How it's enforced audit_events rejects UPDATE and DELETE at the schema layer BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE triggers raise an exception; TestAuditEvents_TableIsAppendOnly runs pool.Exec against the triggers and asserts both fail The repository interface for audit events has no Update / Delete methods A typo in a SQL string can't surface through the interface; review would catch it

docs.title: Network posture
docs.text: Rule How it's enforced The agent accepts no inbound connections for control-plane or user traffic Its only listener serves /healthz, /readyz and /metrics on SB_LOCAL_ADDR. The binary binds 127.0.0.1:8090 by default. The agent Helm chart binds 0.0.0.0:8090 because kubelet probes come from the node, creates no Service, and its default NetworkPolicy denies all ingress (ingress: []). Where the CNI doesn't enforce NetworkPolicy, that probe port is reachable on the pod IP from inside the cluster network. The agent never imports any DB or Redis driver The agent's CI greps go.sum for pgx, lib/pq, redis/go-redis, mongo-driver, etc., and fails the build if any appear core stays infra-free Same go.sum audit on the core repo; no database/sql, no redis/go-redis Plain http:// to the Control Plane is refused by default Agent's validateEndpoint rejects non-https schemes unless SB_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=true is set; loud WARN log at startup if the flag is on

docs.title: Gateway (Release 1, in progress)
docs.text:
The Gateway is optional and its observation path is not merged yet. These rules hold in the merged binary, chart and registry. The full STRIDE analysis is the Gateway threat model.

Rule How it's enforced The Gateway changes nothing it observes Argo CD is read through a transport pinned to the configured origin that allows GET to two paths only; every other method, path and query key is refused before the request leaves the process. The control-plane client refuses any route outside the Gateway endpoints The Gateway never reads Kubernetes Secrets Release 1 has no Kubernetes access: the chart renders no Role and mounts no service-account token. The Release 2 Kubernetes connectors refuse to start if the service account can use any verb on secrets or a write verb on what they read, with no override The control plane cannot redirect the Gateway A task names a connector id and a target id only. Hosts, AppProjects and Applications come from the Gateway's local configuration Gateway and agent credentials are separate Own tables, X-Gateway-Secret header and GatewayAuth middleware. The secret is stored as a SHA-256 hash and compared in constant time Argo CD health is never proof of propagation The Argo CD connector reports at most observed with confidence low and attaches the caveat argocd_health_not_proof. The control plane recomputes every stage outcome from the reported facts, following ADR 0001: a task that saw only Argo CD Healthy and Synced ends unverified with reason context_only, never verified. There is no failed verdict; missing or late evidence ends pending and then timed_out

docs.title: Authentication & authorization
docs.text: Rule How it's enforced Single-shot wrap consumption is atomic MarkConsumed is a single SQL UPDATE with WHERE consumed_at IS NULL; TestRetrieve_ConcurrentAgents_ExactlyOneWins proves 6 racers → exactly one wins Agent secret comparisons are constant-time crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare on every heartbeat path User login is constant-time-ish even on unknown email The auth service runs bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword against a dummy hash when the email isn't found, so an attacker can't enumerate users by latency Generic 401 / 410 / 409 on every failure shape; the audit log carries the specifics Login failures audit actor=anonymous, error_kind=wrong_password and email_length (never the email body; defends against audit-table spam) Users authenticate with the session cookie only Login returns no token and the api ignores Authorization: Bearer for users. The sb_session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict (and Secure outside SB_ENV=dev), and logout, session revocation or disabling the user ends it server-side

docs.title: Threat model: what we defend against
docs.text: Attacker Attack Defense Passive network listener Capture plaintext on the wire TLS minimum; agent refuses http:// by default Compromised system CA bundle Forge cert against your CP Pin a private CA via SB_CP_CA_FILE (replaces system roots, doesn't add) TLS-terminating proxy in a service mesh Read plaintext between TLS termination and the api process Wire envelope: X25519 sealing CP→Agent, KMS-DEK envelope Agent→CP; proxy sees only ciphertext Database exfiltration / stolen backup Read every secret wrap Storage envelope: per-row KMS-wrapped data key; without the KMS the dump is noise Misbehaving CP process logging payloads before encryption Plaintext in app logs Service-layer audits content_hash + byte_length only; handlers strip value fields from logs Concurrent claim race on a wrap Two readers see the same value Atomic MarkConsumed with row lock; second caller gets 410 Gone Replay of an already-consumed wrap Re-fetch a leaked wrap Schema CHECK enforces single-shot; storage-layer test asserts Timing oracle on login Enumerate emails by response time Dummy bcrypt on unknown-email path Forged or stolen user token Sign a token, or replay one copied from a script or log, to act as a user There is no user token to forge: the api reads no bearer token for users. A session is a server-side row behind the HttpOnly cookie, so revoking it or disabling the user stops it on the next request Stale agent claiming after lease expired Double-execution of a job WHERE claimed_by = $4 AND status = 'claimed' on the complete UPDATE; owner mismatch returns 409 Brute force / credential stuffing on /auth/login Guess a local user's password Per-account lockout after 5 consecutive wrong passwords (15 minutes, independent of source IP, kept in Postgres) plus a per-IP limit of 30 attempts per 60s as anti-scan. The per-IP limiter fails open when Redis is unavailable; the lockout does not. See Authentication. Operator deploys with SB_KMS_BACKEND=local in production Storage envelope uses a key that lives in the api's own env The api refuses to boot with local unless SB_ENV=dev, and SB_ENV defaults to production. The secrets-bridge chart refuses kms.backend=local with env=production at render time. Weak or shared local-admin credentials Local password login as the only way in OIDC sign-in (PKCE, group-claim to role mapping, back-channel logout). Local login stays as break-glass, and every successful local sign-in emits a BREAK_GLASS_LOGIN audit event with severity=CRITICAL. Long-lived agent credentials passing through people Copy an agent_secret from a browser, a chat message or a ticket Direct mint (POST /api/v1/agents), which returns the long-lived secret to the admin, answers 403 unless the dev-only SB_ALLOW_DIRECT_AGENT_MINT=true is set. Agents enroll with one-time, hash-only, short-TTL tokens bound to one provider connection; the long-lived credential goes straight to the agent and is never shown to a person.

docs.title: Threat model: what we don't yet defend against (open P0 work)
docs.text:
Attacker Attack Mitigation status Compromised host running the agent Steal the agent credential (the identity file or SB_AGENT_SECRET) Open: the credential is a long-lived bearer secret. Workload identity (SPIFFE / IRSA) and rotation are agent#12 + api#28 KMS master key rotation breaks the platform Operator can't rotate without downtime Open: tested runbook is api#31 Customer admin who controls a Gateway Report false Argo CD state for their own requests Accepted for Release 1: evidence is customer-side attestation, and the design labels it with the Gateway that observed it. Signed evidence is gateway#7 and must ship before Gateway evidence is presented as compliance evidence DBA with direct Postgres access Drop the audit triggers Acknowledged: the schema is a defense; database-level RBAC and audit-log shipping to a separate system are deployment-side responsibilities

Remaining findings from the 2026-09 security assessment are tracked in api#192.

docs.title: What we don't do: by design
docs.text:
• We don't store secret values long-term. Wraps have a TTL measured in minutes / hours. The platform is not a secrets store; it's a governance + access plane on top of one.
  • We don't broker provider credentials. The agent reads its own Vault token / IRSA role from its own environment. The CP never sees them.
  • We don't terminate TLS for the user. The Helm chart wires ingress; the api itself is a plain HTTP server behind that terminator. TLS is mandatory in production but enforced at the network boundary, not inside the api process.
  • We don't sync K8s secrets from the CP. The controller reconciles a CRD via GitOps semantics; the CP itself has no inbound connectivity into any workload cluster.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Catalogues + tables. Look here when you need the exact name of an endpoint, a permission, a provider, or a KMS backend.

Page What HTTP API endpoints Every route the api exposes today, the auth gate, and the response shape Providers supported Vault / AWS SM / GCP SM / Azure Key Vault: auth + config shape per provider KMS backends local / vault-transit / aws-kms: when to use each, env vars Permissions catalog The canonical list of permission strings used by auth.Require(perm)

docs.title: HTTP API endpoints
docs.text:
Every route the api exposes today. Auth column shows what's required to call it.

Auth Meaning public No auth, open route (probes, login) session A signed-in session: the sb_session cookie from /auth/login or a sign-in callback. There are no bearer tokens; scripts keep the cookie in a jar (curl -c jar, then -b jar) session + perm A session + the named permission via auth.Require(perm) agent An agent's X-Agent-Secret header (validated by AgentAuth middleware) gateway A Gateway's X-Gateway-Secret header (validated by GatewayAuth middleware) user_id A ?user_id=<uuid> query param matching the request's requester (stop-gap until OIDC)

docs.title: Probes
docs.text: Method Path Auth Notes GET /healthz public Always 200 GET /readyz public 200 when all readiness checks pass; 503 with per-check failure map otherwise GET /metrics public Prometheus exposition

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/auth/login public {email, password} → {expires_at, user}, and sets the sb_session cookie. No token in the body GET /api/v1/auth/providers public Sign-in buttons for the login page: each enabled console provider, plus the env-var OIDC provider (type: "oidc") when SB_OIDC_ISSUER is set. 120 a minute per IP

docs.title: Sign in with Google
docs.text: Google configured from the console. See Sign in with Google for the flow. "Fresh MFA" means the route also runs RequireFreshMFA and answers 401 step_up_required on a stale session.

docs.title: Sign-in round trip
docs.text: Method Path Auth Notes GET /api/v1/auth/sso/google/start public Redirects to Google. 30 a minute per IP GET /api/v1/auth/sso/google/callback public Google returns here. On success, sets the session cookie and redirects to return_to. Every refusal redirects to /login?error=sso, whatever the reason; the reason is in the audit log as auth.sso.callback error_kind. 60 a minute per IP POST /api/v1/auth/sso/google/connect session + fresh MFA Starts Connect Google for the caller's account. Returns {redirect_url}; the callback comes back to /me#sso_ticket=… POST /api/v1/auth/sso/google/finish session {ticket}. Redeems a Connect or Test ticket, only on the session that started it (403 sso_ticket_refused otherwise). Returns {purpose, result} with result linked, ok or failed (and reason for a failed test). A refused link is 409 link_refused with a reason such as identity_taken GET /api/v1/users/me/identities session Connected accounts: provider_type, email, linked_at DELETE /api/v1/users/me/identities/google session + fresh MFA Disconnect. 409 identity_required when the Google sign-in created the account

docs.title: Sign-in providers and settings
docs.text:
Every route needs a global auth.sso.edit.

Method Path Auth Notes GET /api/v1/sso/providers session + auth.sso.edit List. Each provider has redirect_url (empty until a public address is set) and client_secret_set, never the secret POST /api/v1/sso/providers session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA {type: "google", display_name, client_id, client_secret, allowed_domains, require_approval, default_role_id}. Created turned off. require_approval defaults to true GET /api/v1/sso/providers/:id session + auth.sso.edit One provider PUT /api/v1/sso/providers/:id session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA Edit everything except the secret and enabled. A client_secret field gets 400 PUT /api/v1/sso/providers/:id/secret session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA {client_secret}. Replace the secret POST /api/v1/sso/providers/:id/enable session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA 409 provider_not_ready with missing (public_url, client_secret, allowed_domains) POST /api/v1/sso/providers/:id/disable session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA POST /api/v1/sso/providers/:id/test session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA Starts a Test round trip, also while the provider is off. Returns {redirect_url}; the callback comes back to /admin/sign-in#sso_ticket=… DELETE /api/v1/sso/providers/:id session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA Remove GET /api/v1/sso/settings session + auth.sso.edit public_url, public_url_source (env, console or empty) and pending_cap PUT /api/v1/sso/settings session + auth.sso.edit + fresh MFA {public_url, pending_cap}; either may be left out. 409 public_url_from_env when SB_PUBLIC_URL is set. pending_cap is 1 to 10,000

Stable error codes on these routes:

Code Status Meaning invalid_input 400 A field failed validation; field names it default_role_privileged 400 The default role holds something other than secret.list, secret.request or audit.read default_role_needs_approval_off 400 A default role was set with approval on env_provider_is_google 409 SB_OIDC_ISSUER is already Google provider_exists 409 A Google provider already exists provider_not_ready 409 Turn on is missing something; see missing public_url_from_env 409 The address is set by SB_PUBLIC_URL

docs.title: Accounts waiting for approval
docs.text:
Every route needs a global user_role.edit.

Method Path Auth Notes GET /api/v1/users/pending session + user_role.edit Waiting accounts, oldest first, at most 100, with total for the count POST /api/v1/users/:id/approve session + user_role.edit {role_id, scope}. Grants the role and clears the waiting flag in one transaction. scope uses the POST /user-roles rules; a malformed one gets 400. 409 user_not_pending for an account that isn't waiting POST /api/v1/users/:id/decline session + user_role.edit Disables a waiting account. 409 user_not_pending for any other account

A waiting account may call only GET /api/v1/users/me (which includes pending_approval: true), POST /api/v1/auth/logout and POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/logout. Everything else answers 403 account_pending_approval.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text: Onboarding is self-enrollment by default: an admin mints a one-time, provider-connection-bound enrollment token; the agent exchanges it for its persistent credential. The legacy direct mint is disabled unless explicitly enabled as a break-glass admin action.

docs.title: Onboarding & admin management (session auth + permission)
docs.text: Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/provider-connections/:id/agent-enrollment-token session + agent.mint Mint a one-time, connection-bound enrollment token (returned ONCE) POST /api/v1/agents/enroll enrollment token Exchange the token for a persistent agent_token (returned ONCE); creates a connection-bound agent POST /api/v1/agents session + agent.mint Legacy direct mint, disabled by default → 403 direct_agent_mint_disabled. Break-glass only via SB_ALLOW_DIRECT_AGENT_MINT=true GET /api/v1/agents session + agent.list Thin list. New integrations should prefer the admin/provider projections below GET /api/v1/admin/agents session + agent.list Rich admin list + filters (provider_connection_id, status, cluster_name, provider_type); shows provider_connection_id GET /api/v1/admin/agents/:id session + agent.list Rich admin get GET /api/v1/provider-connections/:id/agents session + agent.list Agents for a provider connection (UI Agents tab) POST /api/v1/admin/agents/:id/revoke session + agent.revoke Revoke with reason → revoked_at/revoked_by; emits agent.revoked audit (agent_id, provider_connection_id, reason) POST /api/v1/agent-enrollment-tokens/:id/revoke session + agent.mint Revoke an UNUSED enrollment token

docs.title: Agent data plane (X-Agent-Secret)
docs.text:
Method Path Auth Notes PUT /api/v1/agents/:id/public-key agent Self-register X25519 wire-envelope pubkey POST /api/v1/agents/:id/heartbeat agent Bodyless → 204 (unchanged). With an optional body (status/agent_version/capabilities) → 200 {status, server_time, next_heartbeat_seconds}. Bumps last_seen_at; first heartbeat flips enrolled→active POST /api/v1/agents/:id/jobs/claim agent 200 with job or 204 (queue empty) POST /api/v1/agents/:id/jobs/:job_id/complete agent {status, error?}; 204 POST /api/v1/agents/:id/dek agent Issue a KMS-wrapped DEK for wire-envelope encryption POST /api/v1/agents/:id/wraps agent Read flow: agent posts a fetched value GET /api/v1/agents/:id/wraps/:wrap_id agent Patch flow: agent retrieves a value (single-shot) POST /api/v1/agents/:id/secrets/bulk agent Discovery: bulk-upsert discovered secrets

Release notes: agent management

  • Heartbeat response shape. A heartbeat with a body now returns 200 {status, server_time, next_heartbeat_seconds}. A bodyless heartbeat keeps the original empty 204. Existing agents are unaffected.
  • Revoke audit action. New revocations emit agent.revoked (metadata: agent_id, provider_connection_id, reason). Legacy audit rows may still carry the older agent.revoke action, so dashboards should alias both.
  • Prefer the admin/provider projections. GET /api/v1/agents remains a thin list. New integrations should use GET /api/v1/admin/agents, GET /api/v1/admin/agents/:id, or GET /api/v1/provider-connections/:id/agents (richer projection incl. provider_connection_id).

docs.title: Gateways
docs.text: Release 1 of the Gateway: the registry and the observation tasks. Install steps are in Gateway. The flow behind the task routes is in Observation flow.

docs.title: Gateway machine routes
docs.text:
The /api/v1/gateways/ prefix is exempt from the session gate. Enrollment is authenticated by the one-time token only; every other route needs X-Gateway-Secret and is rate limited per authenticated Gateway. Errors are {"error": "<code>"} from a closed list and never echo request content.

Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/gateways/enroll enrollment token {enrollment_token, cluster_name?} → 201 {gateway_id, gateway_secret, heartbeat_interval_seconds, claim_poll_seconds}. The secret is returned once. Refused over plain http outside SB_ENV=dev (403 https_required). 10 a minute per IP POST /api/v1/gateways/:id/heartbeat gateway {replica_id, gateway_version, contract_versions, status, in_flight, catalog_version?, connectors?} → {status, server_time, next_heartbeat_seconds, claim_poll_seconds, contract_version, catalog_version}. 429 replica_limit past max_replicas. A replica that reports over_privileged is audited as gateway.over_privileged PUT /api/v1/gateways/:id/catalog gateway Full replace of advertised connectors and targets → {accepted, targets_stale, catalog_version}. Never approves or binds anything. A target no longer advertised stays, marked stale POST /api/v1/gateways/:id/tasks/claim gateway E4. {replica_id, max_tasks: 1} → 200 with one task (task_id, attempt_id, attempt_count, lease_expires_at, deadline_at, request_id, correlation_id, skew_margin_seconds, gateway_scope, connector_refs, expected_change, rollout_baseline), or 204 with Retry-After: 5 when nothing is claimable or no heartbeat has negotiated a contract version yet. Scoped to the authenticated Gateway. 429 inflight_limit with Retry-After when the Gateway is at max_inflight_tasks or the replica already holds a task. 409 contract_version_unsupported. 2400 a minute POST /api/v1/gateways/:id/tasks/:task_id/lease gateway E5. {replica_id, attempt_id} → {lease_expires_at}. Extends the lease by 60s, capped at the deadline. 1200 a minute POST /api/v1/gateways/:id/tasks/:task_id/release gateway E6. {replica_id, attempt_id, reason} with reason one of shutdown, over_capacity, connector_unavailable → 204. The task goes back to the queue. Never counts as a failure. 1200 a minute POST /api/v1/gateways/:id/tasks/:task_id/result gateway E7. A closed-schema evidence result (schema_version, task_id, attempt_id, gateway_id, replica_id, gateway_version, started_at, finished_at, attempt_status, refusal_reason?, stages, clock) → {status, task_state, verdict, next}. status is accepted, or duplicate for the same body sent again for the same attempt. next is none or rescheduled. Body limit 64 KiB. 1200 a minute

A revoked or disabled Gateway gets 401 on every route above. The E4 to E7 rate limits fail closed: without Redis they answer 503, which the Gateway treats as transient. The claim, lease and release bodies are limited to 4 KiB.

Task route error codes:

Status Code Meaning 400 invalid_request Malformed body, unknown field, or ids that do not match the path 401 unauthorized The Gateway is not live (revoked or disabled) 404 not_found Unknown task, or a task of another Gateway 409 attempt_superseded The attempt is not the task's current one: its lease ran out and the task was claimed again, it was released, or the Gateway was revoked or disabled while it held the lease 409 lease_expired The lease ended before the call 409 task_closed The task is closed (done, dead, cancelled), or its deadline passed and this call closed it as timed_out 409 result_conflict A different body for an attempt whose result was already accepted 409 contract_version_unsupported None of the Gateway's contract versions is the one tasks are written in 422 schema_violation The result is outside the closed schema, names a stage the task does not expect, or fails the evidence binding 422 evidence_out_of_window started_at, finished_at or observed_at is outside the attempt, allowing for clock skew 429 inflight_limit Claim only: the Gateway or the replica is at its in-flight limit

docs.title: Gateway admin routes (session auth + permission)
docs.text:
Every write also needs a fresh second factor.

Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/admin/gateways session + gateway.mint + fresh MFA {name, boundary, environment_id?, max_replicas?, max_inflight_tasks?} → 201, status pending. 409 gateway_name_taken GET /api/v1/admin/gateways session + gateway.list {items: [...]} with status (pending, active, stale, disabled, revoked), versions, last heartbeat and replica count. Never credentials GET /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id session + gateway.list {gateway, replicas, connectors, bindings, enrollment_tokens}, metadata only POST /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id/enrollment-token session + gateway.mint + fresh MFA {expires_in_seconds?, expected_cluster_name?} → 201 {id, gateway_id, enrollment_token, expires_at}. The token is returned once. Default TTL 900s, clamped to 60 to 86400. 409 gateway_not_pending once enrolled POST /api/v1/admin/gateway-enrollment-tokens/:id/revoke session + gateway.mint + fresh MFA Revoke an unused token. 204 POST /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id/revoke session + gateway.revoke + fresh MFA {reason?} → the Gateway, status revoked. 409 gateway_already_revoked POST /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id/connectors/:cid/approve session + gateway.bind + fresh MFA :cid is the connector's id. 409 connector_not_advertised POST /api/v1/admin/gateway-bindings session + gateway.bind + fresh MFA {gateway_id, environment_id, project_id?, secret_id \| (provider_connection_id + secret_ref), argocd_connector_id, argocd_target_id, observation_timeout_seconds?} → 201. Argo CD targets only in Release 1 GET /api/v1/admin/gateway-bindings session + gateway.bind Optional ?gateway_id= DELETE /api/v1/admin/gateway-bindings/:id session + gateway.bind + fresh MFA 204. Cancels the binding's open tasks (binding_removed) PUT /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id/enabled session + gateway.revoke + fresh MFA {enabled} → the Gateway. Disable refuses its calls with 401 and moves its leased tasks back to queued. Enable returns it to active, or pending if it never enrolled. 409 gateway_revoked GET /api/v1/admin/gateways/:id/tasks session + gateway.list {items, counts}. Optional ?state= (queued, leased, done, dead, cancelled) and ?limit= (1 to 500, default 100). Each item has state, verdict, verdict_reason, attempt_count, failure_count, not_before, deadline_at and ids, never secret values GET /api/v1/admin/environments/:id/observation-source session + gateway.bind {environment_id, observation_source}. 404 environment_not_found PUT /api/v1/admin/environments/:id/observation-source session + gateway.bind + fresh MFA {observation_source} with control_plane, gateway or none → {environment_id, observation_source, previous_observation_source, tasks_cancelled}. Leaving gateway cancels the environment's open tasks (source_changed). 400 invalid_observation_source

Audit actions, all with ids, enums and counts only: gateway.create, gateway.enrollment_token.create, gateway.enrollment_token.revoke, gateway.enroll, gateway.revoke, gateway.auth.rejected, gateway.replica_limit, gateway.over_privileged, gateway.catalog.updated, gateway.connector.missing, gateway.connector.approval_reset, gateway.connector.approved, gateway.binding.create, gateway.binding.delete, gateway.enable, gateway.disable and environment.observation_source.update.

Observation audit actions: observation.task.created, observation.task.claimed, observation.task.released, observation.task.lease_expired, observation.evidence.accepted, observation.evidence.rejected (with a reason), gateway.evidence.outcome_mismatch, observation.task.verdict, observation.task.dead, observation.task.timed_out, observation.task.superseded, observation.task.cancelled and request.observation_skipped (with a reason such as no_gateway_binding or source_none).

docs.title: Requests (access requests)
docs.text: Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/requests session Submit a patch request POST /api/v1/requests/read session Submit a read request GET /api/v1/requests session List with ?requester_id + ?status filters GET /api/v1/requests/:id session Get one + inline approvals POST /api/v1/requests/:id/approve session {approver_id, comment?} POST /api/v1/requests/:id/reject session {approver_id, reason} POST /api/v1/requests/:id/cancel session {actor_id} (only the requester) GET /api/v1/requests/:id/wraps user_id List value-free wrap summaries GET /api/v1/requests/:id/wraps/:wrap_id user_id Single-shot retrieve (consumes) GET /api/v1/requests/:id/gitops user_id BRD §26 observation list (404 when feature is off) GET /api/v1/requests/:id/observations session Gateway evidence for the request, behind the same read check as GET /requests/:id: {observation_source, rollup, label, tasks}. rollup is none (no task), pending, verified, partially_observed, unverified or timed_out. label is always observed_operational_state. Each task has gateway_name, state, verdict, verdict_reason, deadline_at and stages; each stage has outcome, reported_outcome, observed_at, connector_id, target_id, caveats and facts. Argo CD stages always carry argocd_health_not_proof. Resource names are not included. Tasks past their deadline are closed as timed_out before the read

docs.title: Cross-team requests
docs.text:
Slice N: Team A → Team B value handoff. See Cross-team requests for the operator model, state machine, and SoD matrix.

Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/requests/cross-team session + secret.request {target_team_id, target_project_id, target_environment_id, destination_provider_connection_id, destination_secret_ref, destination_keys[], justification} → AccessRequest. Refuses min_approvers ≥ 2 with cross_team_min_approvers_unsupported. NO values in body. destination_keys is the NAME list. POST /api/v1/requests/:id/fill session + secret.value.provide {key_values: {<key>: base64}, fill_comment?}. Late writers get fill_window_expired (410). Same-actor-as-requester returns separation_of_duties_violated (403). POST /api/v1/requests/:id/refuse session + secret.value.provide {reason} (≥ 10 chars). Transitions to refused. POST /api/v1/requests/:id/verify session + secret.approve or secret.security.approve {decision, voted_as, comment?} → 200 OK with structured VerifyResponse (NOT 412 on partial votes). Body: {vote_recorded, voted_as, source_votes, security_approval_required, security_vote_present, next_required[]}. GET /api/v1/requests/inbox session + secret.value.provide ?team_id= narrows to one team's inbox. Returns AccessRequest[] with pending_values status. Fail-closed: empty array when caller covers no teams. GET /api/v1/requests/inbox/count session + secret.value.provide {total, per_team: [{team_id, team_name?, count}]}. Drives the sidebar badge. GET /api/v1/provider-connections?project_id=:id session Returns the connections bound to that project; the SPA's cross-team submit drawer hits this for the source project's destination dropdown.

docs.title: VerifyResponse routing
docs.text:
The structured response means the SPA can render the right next-step toast without a second round trip:

Scenario voted_as security_approval_required security_vote_present next_required[] Source vote, no security required source false false [] (transitions to approved) Source vote, security required, not yet voted source true false ["security_approval"]: SPA toast "your source vote was recorded; security approval still pending" Security vote, source already voted security true true [] (transitions to approved)

The SPA's crossTeamErrorMessage(code) maps the stable 403 codes to friendly strings; see the table at the bottom of Cross-team requests.

docs.title: Reveal sessions
docs.text:
Slice M: bulk reveal page surface. Open returns wrap_id + key_name handles; the SPA loops over them calling the single-shot /requests/:id/wraps/:wrap_id retrieve for each plaintext. See Reveal sessions for the operator guide.

Method Path Auth Notes POST /api/v1/reveal-sessions session + step-up MFA {access_request_id} → {session_id, expires_at, ttl_seconds, wraps[]}. 20/60s per identity rate limit. GET /api/v1/reveal-sessions/me/active session Caller's active sessions; value-free summaries (no envelopes) POST /api/v1/reveal-sessions/:id/expire session {reason: 'user_hide' \| 'unmount'} → 204; owner-bound; idempotent server-side

docs.title: Workflows / Policies / Roles / Assignments / Tenancy (admin)
docs.text: Method Path Auth POST /api/v1/roles session + role.edit GET /api/v1/roles session GET /api/v1/roles/:id session PUT /api/v1/roles/:id/permissions session + role.edit DELETE /api/v1/roles/:id session + role.edit POST /api/v1/user-roles session + user_role.edit GET /api/v1/user-roles session DELETE /api/v1/user-roles/:id session + user_role.edit GET /api/v1/users/:userID/roles session POST /api/v1/workflows session + workflow.edit GET /api/v1/workflows session GET /api/v1/workflows/scoped-policy-authorable session + policy.author at any scope GET /api/v1/workflows/:id session PUT /api/v1/workflows/:id session + workflow.edit DELETE /api/v1/workflows/:id session + workflow.edit POST /api/v1/policies session + policy.edit GET /api/v1/policies session GET /api/v1/policies/:id session PUT /api/v1/policies/:id session + policy.edit DELETE /api/v1/policies/:id session + policy.edit POST /api/v1/projects session GET /api/v1/projects session GET /api/v1/projects/:id session PUT /api/v1/projects/:id/status session GET /api/v1/projects/:id/environments session POST /api/v1/environments session GET /api/v1/environments session DELETE /api/v1/environments/:id session
